Performers
Mainzer Kammerorchester (orchestra), Günter Kehr (conductor) Documented

The side-two label gives these performers specifically for the symphony. Martin Galling, Klaus Pohlers, Georg Schmid and Reinhold Buhl are credited separately for the quartet on the same side; the item-wide list of artists is therefore insufficient to identify the symphony’s individual players.

[2] [1]
Work version
Original string-orchestra work, all three movements Documented

The original label identifies Symphony No. 5 in B minor and lists all three movements. The score has two violin parts, viola and figured bass. The edition, continuo realisation and orchestral parts used in this session are unknown. The modern critical edition supplies the musical observations; it postdates the recording.

[2] [4] [7]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

No session date is established. The January 1961 review provides a documented upper bound; the Archive dates the issue 1959 and the sleeve bears a 1959 copyright notice. The 2022 scan and transfer dates concern the archival copy.

[1] [2] [10]
Place
Germany Documented

The original side-two label states ‘Rec. in Germany’. City, venue and studio are unknown.

[2]
Label
Vox Documented

Monaural US vinyl LP, The Sons of Bach, Vol. I: Symphonies and Chamber Music. The sleeve bears a 1959 Vox Productions copyright notice.

[2] [1]
Catalogue
DL 463-1 Documented

Catalogue number printed on the sleeve and both labels, matching the Internet Archive carrier metadata.

[2] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 2, band 1; printed side identifiers DL 463-1 B and M-1118-B Documented

These identifiers are transcribed from the label. Runout inscriptions, stamper, session take and original tape number are unknown. The label gives the symphony’s duration as 12:33; the selected digital transfer lasts 758.93 seconds.

[2] [3]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP transfer; operator account associate-klentjohn-postanes Documented

The operator is identified only by the archive account. The sleeve’s separate credit ‘Mastering: Dr. R. van Gelder’ concerns the historical LP.

[1] [2]
Transfer date
2022-10-29 Documented

Transcribed from ripping_date 20221029092156. The artwork scan is dated 26 October 2022. Neither date identifies the performance session.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; 24-bit FLAC side transfer and segmented VBR MP3 derivative. Documented

Equipment comes from the item’s lineage field; the file list identifies the FLAC side and MP3 track. Equalisation, de-clicking, pitch correction and noise reduction settings are unknown.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms. Inferred, not documented

Bach composed the symphony in 1773 and died in 1788. Copyright in the modern critical edition is separate; its score is cited for research and is not reproduced here.

[8] [5]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: lawful commercial publication no later than January 1961, before 1963. Documented

HiFi/Stereo Review reviewed this exact Vox catalogue and performance in January 1961. Internet Archive dates the issue 1959, corroborated by the sleeve’s 1959 copyright notice, but the rights assessment uses the independently documented 1961 publication bound. Under the project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule, the former 50-year phonogram term expired before the extension applied on 1 November 2013. US recording rights remain unestablished. Internet Archive supplies no Creative Commons licence. Clearance here is territorial, not worldwide.

Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach, Symphony in B minor, Wq 182/5; Mainzer Kammerorchester, Günter Kehr. Vox DL 463-1 (mono, dated 1959; commercially available by January 1961), side 2, band 1; Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established.

Page 4: side-two label, band 1, all three symphony movements, Mainzer Kammerorchester, Günter Kehr, ‘Rec. in Germany’, DL 463-1 B and M-1118-B. Label and sleeve inspected visually. Robert Cushman’s sleeve notes incorrectly describe the Wq 182 symphonies as published in 1773; the modern critical introduction establishes their manuscript circulation.. Accessed 2026-10-18.

Openings of all three movements, Larghetto dynamics on pp. 67–⁠68, and Presto repeat signs and ending on pp. 70 and 73 inspected visually. Musical cues describe whole movements or their opening paragraphs; no bar-by-bar timing or ear review is asserted.. Accessed 2026-10-18.

Sarah Adams — introduction to Six Symphonies for Baron van Swieten — Pp. xi–xii: Hamburg, 1773, scoring and commission; pp. xii–xiv: Reichardt’s 1814 recollection of the trial performance at Büsch’s house; pp. xiv–xv: Westphal’s 1777 catalogue, 1789 letter and later publication history.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  6. Peter Wollny — preface to the C. P. E. Bach symphonies — Three-movement design, binary finales with repeated halves, continuo scoring and the 1773 van Swieten set.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  7. IMSLP — Symphony in B minor, H.661 — Catalogue equivalence Wq 182/5 and H.661; key, 1773 composition date, scoring and the three movement titles.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  8. C. P. E. Bach: The Complete Works — chronology — 1773 lists Wq 182/5; 14 December 1788 records the composer’s death.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  9. AWA — Mainz Chamber Orchestra / Günter Kehr reissue track listing — Lists the three Kehr movements as 4:30, 3:44 and 4:20. These rounded durations corroborate the broad movement divisions around 4:36 and 8:22 in the selected LP transfer; they do not supply bar-level alignment. The reissue calls movement I Allegro, while the original Vox label and critical score give Allegretto.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  10. HiFi/Stereo Review, January 1961 — review of Vox DL 463-1 — Printed and PDF p. 58: B minor and D major symphonies, Mainzer Kammerorchester, Günter Kehr, Vox DL 463-1 and retail price. The issue cover dates the review January 1961. Establishes commercial publication before 1963 independently of the sleeve copyright notice.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
